accuracy.evidence: Checked against Rosenshine (2012) Principles of Instruction, American Educator (principle 1: begin a lesson with a short review of previous learning), Roediger and Karpicke (2006) on the testing effect (recall beats restudy for later retention), Dunlosky et al. (2013) rating practice testing highly useful, and the EEF (2021) Cognitive science approaches in the classroom review. The lab's bar numbers (overnight drop to 50-65%, +35 for recall, +25 for a checked wrong try, +5 for a peek) are labelled in the adult text as an illustration of the ordering recall > corrected error > restudy, not as measured values. Arithmetic (7 + 3 = 10, 17 + 3 = 20, 15 - 3 = 12) checked.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented retrieval-practice slips named in the adult text: forgetting seen as failure (predict 1, night scene shows bars fall but not to zero, p5, m9, challenge 'forgot'), starting with new work (order scene refuses New work in slot 1, p1, challenge 'newfirst'), peeking or rereading instead of recalling (predict 2, peek adds only 5, p3, m4, m8, challenge 'peek'/'reread'), stopping after a wrong answer (a wrong recall is checked and still adds 25, m1, challenge 'wrongstop') and an over-long look back (predict 3, slider feedback at 4+, m2, challenge 'long').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagwarmup is built on the session-start routine itself: a draggable moon that drives an overnight forgetting animation on three memory bars, a three-slot session timeline that only accepts the look back first, per-fact 'from memory' versus 'peek' choices with unequal strength gains, a slider that splits a 15-minute practice bar between look back and new work, and a new question (17 + 3) that is solved from the warmed-up fact. 242 Testing yourself (flagrecall) is a flashcard/Leitner lab, 449 Spacing out practice (flagspaced) schedules gaps over days, and 391 (flaglookback) is reflection after learning; lab shingle similarity is under 30% against every flag_*.js (lab_distinct gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each part by acting: dragging the moon shows the bars sink to 60%, 50% and 65% but stay above zero; New work dropped in slot 1 is refused with the reason; peeking moves a bar by only 5 while a recall jumps it 35 and a checked wrong answer still adds 25, so the only way to reach 80% is recall; the slider's practice bar visibly loses new-work minutes as questions rise; and 17 + 3 is solved from the lit 7 + 3 = 10 card. Done messages restate the rule only after it has been seen.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Yes, just as easy' (the bars drop overnight), 'Peeking at the answer' (peek gains 5 against 35 for recall) and 'Yes, look back at everything' (the slider shows a long look back eating the new-work time and is marked too long).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions whose wrong options carry seven distinct slip messages: newfirst (new work first leaves yesterday cold), peek (feels easy, hardly strengthens), reread (rereading helps less than recall), forgot (forgetting overnight is normal), wrongstop (check and fix, the mistake is useful), long (keep it to 2 or 3) and none (skipping leaves yesterday behind).

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs with everyday words (look back, from memory, check, fix, new work) and passes the kid readability limit in validate_lessons; lab labels are short (from memory, peek, slot 1, 3 questions), and the adult text uses the precise terms (daily review, retrieval practice, forgetting curve, prior knowledge, low-stakes) within the adult limit.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph gives one step of the routine and its reason; adult paragraphs give the research basis with named sources, the mechanism (retrieval strengthens and activates prior knowledge), named mistakes with a low-stakes caution, and what the lab does with its numbers. No content-gate filler phrase matches; lab text is only instructions and feedback.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: the night scene's three fact cards and bars are readable, the three session slots and blocks fit in rows of three with two-line labels, the recall rows show the question on top with the bar and percentage on the left and the 'from memory' and 'peek' buttons on the right without overlap (fixed after the first screenshot showed the percentage under the button), the slider numbers 0-10 and the 15-minute bar fit, and the 17 + 3 tiles and reason cards are full width. walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin (Pass the night; pick a block then a slot; from memory / peek / each answer per fact with aria-labels naming the question; One fewer / One more for the slider; the 17 + 3 answers and the three reasons). The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each scene description and all feedback, the challenge uses a role=status live region, right and wrong cards carry ✓ / ✗ text as well as colour, the memory percentage is printed as a number, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found nothing in light or dark on desktop or phone.

sources: Rosenshine, B. (2012) Principles of Instruction: Research-based strategies that all teachers should know. American Educator 36(1), 12-19
Roediger, H. L. and Karpicke, J. D. (2006) Test-enhanced learning: taking memory tests improves long-term retention. Psychological Science 17(3), 249-255
Dunlosky, J. et al. (2013) Improving students' learning with effective learning techniques. Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1), 4-58
Education Endowment Foundation (2021) Cognitive science approaches in the classroom: a review of the evidence
